dispositions.rationale: 'More notice than the minimum is always safe; less is not' overstates what Civil Code §827 actually establishes — longer notice doesn't cure an otherwise unlawful increase or a defective service. Removed the absolute assurance and replaced it with the correct, narrower point. Also linked the Civil Code §827 citation directly per the review's suggested fix.
dispositions.change_applied: Deleted 'More notice than the minimum is always safe; less is not.' Replaced with 'Serving more than the minimum notice period doesn't by itself cure an otherwise unlawful increase or defective service — the increase still has to be lawful and properly served regardless of notice length.' Civil Code §827 now links to leginfo.legislature.ca.gov.
dispositions.quote_before: More notice than the minimum is always safe; less is not.
dispositions.quote_after: Serving more than the minimum notice period doesn't by itself cure an otherwise unlawful increase or defective service — the increase still has to be lawful and properly served regardless of notice length.

dispositions.rationale: New finding this round: the unqualified 'applying Oakland's higher rate to a Richmond unit is an overcharge' ignores the article's own banking exception (a Richmond owner with banked AGAs can lawfully apply more than 1.5%, potentially up to 6.5%). Qualified the claim exactly as the review suggested.
dispositions.change_applied: 'applying Oakland's higher rate to a Richmond unit is an overcharge that a tenant can challenge...' replaced with 'applying Oakland's 2.3% to a Richmond unit without a lawful banking basis or other authorized exception produces an increase above what Richmond's own cap allows, which a tenant can challenge through Richmond's own petition process.'
dispositions.quote_before: applying Oakland's higher rate to a Richmond unit is an overcharge that a tenant can challenge through Richmond's own petition process.
dispositions.quote_after: applying Oakland's 2.3% to a Richmond unit without a lawful banking basis or other authorized exception produces an increase above what Richmond's own cap allows, which a tenant can challenge through Richmond's own petition process.

dispositions.rationale: The review cited FY 2026–27 Master Fee Schedule p.14 (https://www.ci.richmond.ca.us/DocumentCenter/View/80176) giving current RRIP fees as $110 registration / $220 initial inspection / $94 re-inspection, versus the $106/$211/$90 figures pulled from the FY2025–26 schedule last round. I attempted to independently verify this against the primary PDF and the city's Billing and RRIP pages myself (WebFetch on ci.richmond.ca.us and richmondca.gov, both blocked by robots.txt; WebSearch found no independent secondary source quoting the new figures) and could not confirm it directly. Given the source is specifically a newer, dated fiscal-year document and the prior figures are already known to be one cycle stale, I've updated the post to the cited FY2026–27 amounts as the best available information, but this is flagged below as needing a human check since I couldn't verify it myself. On frequency: the review points out that the repo's own knowledge file doesn't actually resolve which registration-fee-frequency statement is authoritative (a July 2025 dated fee summary doesn't necessarily postdate the January 2025 amendment the way I assumed last round). Rather than assert either version, the post now omits the specific frequency claim and tells the reader to confirm with the Rent Program directly.
dispositions.change_applied: Key Facts RRIP row and the Business License/RRIP body item both updated to $110/$220/$94 (FY 2026–27 fee schedule), with the annual-vs-every-3-years frequency claim removed and replaced with a direct pointer to confirm with the Rent Program.
dispositions.quote_before: a $106/owner registration fee — charged annually for owners of 3 or more units, every three years for owners of 1–2 units — plus a $211/unit inspection fee at the start of each 3-year inspection cycle, with re-inspection at $90/unit if a unit fails.
dispositions.quote_after: a $110/owner registration fee plus a $220/unit inspection fee at the start of each inspection cycle, with re-inspection at $94/unit if a unit fails — per the city's FY 2026–27 fee schedule. How often the registration fee itself recurs ... isn't consistently stated across the city's own published materials, so confirm the current cycle directly with the Rent Program.
